title: Bob Brier's examination suggests Tutankhamun died from a blow to the back of the head

tellings.quote: So, um, Dr. [clears throat] Bob Brier did uh did an investigation on him maybe back in the 90s and examined his body and the way that the pool the way that the blood pulls in the back of his skull looks like he was hit in the back of the head.

plain: Tutankhamun, the boy king of ancient Egypt, may have died from a blow to the back of the head, according to an examination of his body by a scholar named Bob Brier, perhaps in the 1990s. The researcher Luke Caverns passes it on from Brier's work: the way the blood pooled at the back of the skull looked, he says, like the king had been hit there. If so, the king may have been killed rather than dying of natural causes.
